Load the libraries

library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
options(scipen = 999)

Data

For this homework, we are going to use the Gapminder data on population (pop), GDP per capita (gdp), and life expectancy (lex). These data were downloaded and compiled using the gapminder_compile.Rmd script in the data folder.

Let’s focus our attention on data from the past 100 years, between 1925 and 2025.

gapminder <- read_csv("data/gapminder.csv") %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  filter(between(year, 1925, 2025))
  1. Use the function(s) of your choice to get an idea of the overall structure of the data, including its dimensions, column names, classes, etc.
names(gapminder)
## [1] "country" "year"    "pop"     "gdp"     "lex"
glimpse(gapminder)

  1. Which five countries have had the largest absolute population growth between 1925-2025? Show this as a table. #population of 2025-1925 for every country, mutate India, China, Indonesia, Pakistan, USA
top_5 <- gapminder %>% 
  filter(year %in% c(1925,2025)) %>% 
  select(country, year, pop) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = pop) %>% 
  mutate(growth=`2025`-`1925`) %>% 
  arrange(desc(growth)) %>% 
  slice_head(n=5)
top_5

  1. Make a plot that shows population growth over time for the top country you found in question #3.
gapminder %>%
  filter(country == "India") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = pop)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue") +
  labs(title = "Population Growth Over Time - India",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Population")

  1. Has global life expectancy changed between 1925 and 2025? Show the min, median, mean, and max for all countries (combined) in the dataset.
life_expectancy <- gapminder %>%
  filter(year %in% c(1925, 2025)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    min_lex = min(lex, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_lex = median(lex, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_lex = mean(lex, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_lex = max(lex, na.rm = TRUE))
life_expectancy
## # A tibble: 2 × 5
##    year min_lex median_lex mean_lex max_lex
##   <dbl>   <dbl>      <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>
## 1  1925    21.0       35.9     38.1    63.5
## 2  2025    52.8       74.8     73.9    85.6
  1. Make a plot that shows the distribution of life expectancy for all countries in 1925 and 2025 (try using geom_density). What do you notice about the shift in life expectancy over time? Life expectancy has grown a lot, and there is a higher desity of older population in 2025 than 1925.
gapminder %>%
  filter(year %in% c(1925, 2025)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = lex, fill = factor(year))) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Life Expectancy: 1925 vs 2025",
    x = "Life Expectancy",
    y = "Density",
    fill = "Year") +
  theme_classic()
## Warning: Removed 13 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_density()`).

  1. We are interested in the relationship between per capita GDP and life expectancy; i.e. does having more money help you live longer in 2025? Show this as a plot. (Suggestion! Remove Monaco as an extreme outlier.) There is a positive relationship between per captia GDP and life expectancy.
gapminder %>%
  filter(year == 2025, country != "Monaco") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = gdp, y = lex)) +
  geom_point(color = "blue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Relationship Between GDP and Life Expectancy",
    x = "GDP",
    y = "Life Expectancy") +
  theme_classic()
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'
## Warning: Removed 2 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_smooth()`).
## Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

  1. Which five countries have had the highest absolute GDP per capita growth over the past 50 years? Show this as a table. (Suggestion! Remove Monaco as an extreme outlier.) Singapore, Ireland, Luxembourg, Guyana, Norway
gdp_growth <- gapminder %>%
  filter(year %in% c(1975, 2025), country != "Monaco") %>%
  select(country, year, gdp) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = gdp) %>% 
  mutate(gdp_growth = `2025` - `1975`) %>%                     
  arrange(desc(gdp_growth)) %>%                                 
  slice_head(n = 5)                                           
gdp_growth
## # A tibble: 5 × 4
##   country    `1975`  `2025` gdp_growth
##   <chr>       <dbl>   <dbl>      <dbl>
## 1 Singapore  12896. 137906.    125010.
## 2 Ireland    14336. 119406.    105071.
## 3 Luxembourg 30950. 131038.    100088.
## 4 Guyana      5071.  79371.     74300.
## 5 Norway     25513.  94896.     69382.
  1. How does per capita GDP growth compare between these same five countries over the past 50 years? Show this as a plot.
five_countries <- gdp_growth$country
gapminder %>%
  filter(country %in% five_countries, year >= 1975) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = gdp, color = country)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(title = "GDP per Capita Growth Over the Past 50 Years",
    x = "Year",
    y = "GDP per Capita",
    color = "Country") +
  theme_classic()

  1. Do one analysis of your choice that includes a table and plot as outputs. Relationship between life expectancy and population size.
top5_pop <- gapminder %>%
  filter(year == 2025) %>%
  arrange(desc(pop)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5) %>%
  select(country, pop, lex, gdp)
top5_pop
## # A tibble: 5 × 4
##   country          pop   lex    gdp
##   <chr>          <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>
## 1 India     1463865525  72.4 10608.
## 2 China     1416096094  78.8 25505.
## 3 USA        347275807  79.8 78389.
## 4 Indonesia  285721236  72.2 15391.
## 5 Pakistan   255219554  66.7  5717.
gapminder %>%
  filter(year == 2025) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = pop, y = lex)) +
  geom_point(color = "darkgreen", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "red") +
  scale_x_log10() + 
  labs(title = "Life Expectancy vs Population Size (2025)",
    x = "Population (log scale)",
    y = "Life Expectancy") +
  theme_classic()
